title: Frontend / CLI / Protocol Surface Roadmap v1

items.title: Cross-Surface Authority Spine v1 — Canonicalize effective yesterday
items.description: Canonicalize the cross-surface authority spine as enforceable doctrine. Create the canonical doctrine artifact declaring surface rules, protocol rules, forbidden bypasses, implementation sequencing, do-not-overrun guards, and per-surface required tests. This is not advisory — it is the governance spine all future surface work must obey, effective immediately (retroactive to 2026-05-20). Without canonical doctrine, surface-specific implementation will fracture governance.
expected_tests: Schema validation for canonical authority spine artifact
Cross-reference all 14 surface audit artifacts against authority spine rules
Verify all 10 forbidden bypasses documented with blocking status
items.implementation_risk: low — this is a doctrine/docs/schema alignment mission, not feature implementation

items.title: Surface inventory and authority taxonomy (completed — now canonicalized by Cross-Surface Authority Spine v1)
items.description: Catalog every external surface (Frontend/Cockpit, CLI, MCP, ACP, A2A, WebSocket, static docs) with authority tiers, identity models, and maturity ratings. Without this taxonomy, surface-specific governance is impossible and composition risk is invisible. This audit is the prerequisite for all other roadmap items.
expected_tests: Schema validation for all surface taxonomy artifacts
Cross-reference integrity between audit, map, register, and test strategy

items.title: Common envelope and schema spine for all protocol surfaces
items.description: Define a shared JSON envelope schema that every protocol surface (MCP, ACP, A2A, WebSocket) MUST use for structured responses. Without a common envelope, each surface invents its own error format, making cross-surface governance impossible. The envelope carries event_sha256, surface_authority_tier, and content_light flags.
expected_tests: Every protocol response validates against common envelope schema
Error responses conform to envelope contract across all surfaces

items.title: Frontend intent hardening: status indicators and trust spine gating
items.description: Implement all 9 cockpit status indicators as backend-enforced projection fields, not frontend-inferred. Wire trust spine gating into WebSocket message handling so the frontend cannot bypass approval for mutation intents. The frontend remains a dumb renderer; all policy lives in the backend.
expected_tests: All 9 status indicators surface correctly in projection
Trust spine rejects forged approval tokens from frontend
Frontend cannot mutate projection to show false approval state

items.title: CLI command taxonomy unification with dry-run defaults
items.description: Unify all CLI entry points (rig-relay, rig-relay-acp, rig-relay-cockpit, rig-relay-ide-sidecar) under a shared command taxonomy with consistent flags, exit codes, and structured output. Every CLI command must default to dry-run-safe behavior and produce JSON output unless interactive mode is requested.
expected_tests: All entry points share consistent --dry-run and --output flags
Exit codes match documented semantic contract
JSON output validates against entry-point-specific schemas

items.title: MCP read-only surface hardening: real tool dispatch, descriptor integrity, content-light scanning
items.description: Harden the MCP read-only tier with real tool dispatch (not stub responses), enforced descriptor integrity (reject tampered tool manifests), and content-light output scanning (no secrets in tool responses). This is the first protocol surface that external hosts connect to; it must be production-grade before any mutation tier is exposed.
expected_tests: MCP tool dispatch returns real results for all 16 governed tools
Tampered tool descriptor triggers rejection and telemetry
Content-light scanner redacts secrets from tool responses
Roots boundary enforced per-tool and per-session

items.title: Scripts governance gating prevents CLI bypass of cockpit approval
items.description: Implement governance gate that blocks CLI-invoked mutations while cockpit approval is pending or denied. Scripts must not be able to bypass the human-in-the-loop approval flow that the cockpit enforces. This closes a critical side-channel where automation could mutate the workspace without operator consent.
expected_tests: CLI mutation blocked while cockpit approval is pending
CLI mutation blocked when cockpit approval was denied
Governance gate emits telemetry event on rejection
Gate does not block read-only CLI operations

items.title: CLI evidence pack and admin commands with structured output
items.description: Build a CLI evidence pack: commands that produce structured JSON/JSONL evidence artifacts (not Markdown). Include admin commands for session management, fleet status, and coordination state. All output must be schema-validated and machine-consumable for downstream analytics.
expected_tests: All evidence commands produce JSON output
No evidence command produces Markdown
Admin commands respect RBAC boundaries
Output validates against evidence schemas

items.title: Cockpit status indicators: all 9 states implemented and tested
items.description: Complete the implementation of all 9 cockpit status indicators as defined in the trust spine gating spec. Each indicator must be a backend-projected field with clear enumeration, tested for cross-state transitions, and validated against the projection schema.
expected_tests: All 9 status indicator states render correctly
State transitions produce correct projection diffs
Invalid state transitions are rejected by backend
Status indicators survive WebSocket reconnect

items.title: MCP per-user authorization enforcement
items.description: Enforce per-user authorization scoping on MCP server sessions. Each authenticated user session must only access tools and resources scoped to that user's RBAC profile. Cross-tenant or cross-user tool access must be blocked and logged.
expected_tests: User A cannot access User B scoped tools
RBAC profile changes take effect within session
Auth boundary violations emit telemetry

items.title: ACP transport server implementation integrated with governance engine
items.description: Build the ACP transport server that integrates with the governance engine and RuntimeSupervisor. The server must enforce mission scope, session lifecycle, and permission gating as defined in the ACP spec. This is the editor-integrated surface; it must match the governance guarantees of the cockpit.
expected_tests: ACP session lifecycle matches spec
Mission scope enforcement rejects out-of-scope tools
Permission gating mirrors cockpit approval flow
Cancellation and timeout release all resources

items.title: IDE sidecar convergence with ACP transport
items.description: Converge the IDE sidecar IPC protocol with the ACP transport protocol so that IDE-hosted agent sessions share the same governance spine as standalone ACP sessions. The 42 IDE capabilities defined in the manifest must map cleanly to ACP tool scopes.
expected_tests: IDE sidecar messages validate against ACP message schema
All 42 IDE capabilities map to ACP tool scopes
Governance engine applies same rules to IDE and standalone ACP sessions

items.title: Protocol composition risk tests
items.description: Implement the 7 composition risk tests from the test strategy (surf-test-029 through surf-test-035). These tests verify that cross-surface escalation paths are blocked: MCP-to-GitHub, A2A-to-GitHub, frontend-to-MCP, ACP-to-subagent, hosted-to-debug, SSH-to-local, and static-docs-to-public leaks.
expected_tests: All 7 composition risk tests implemented and passing
Cross-surface escalation paths blocked at governance spine
Telemetry emitted for every blocked composition attack

items.title: A2A Agent Card discovery and attestation
items.description: Implement A2A Agent Card discovery with cryptographic attestation. Remote agents must publish signed agent cards with declared trust tiers. Local A2A client must verify signatures, validate trust tier claims, and reject cards that fail attestation.
expected_tests: Valid agent card with signature passes attestation
Tampered agent card rejected
Trust tier mismatch triggers downgrade
Expired card rejected

items.title: MCP resources and prompts real backend wiring
items.description: Wire MCP resources and prompts to real backend data sources instead of stub responses. Resources must reflect live coordination state, fleet status, and evidence artifacts. Prompts must be governed and receipt-backed like tools.
expected_tests: MCP resources return live data from coordination store
MCP prompts are governed by same permission model as tools
Resource and prompt responses are content-light scanned

items.title: SSH read-only diagnostics: command allowlist, key management, session recording
items.description: Design and implement an SSH read-only diagnostics surface with a strict command allowlist, SSH key management, and session recording. This surface allows remote operators to run diagnostic commands without mutation capability. All sessions must be recorded for audit.
expected_tests: Allowlisted commands execute successfully
Non-allowlisted commands rejected
Session recording captures full transcript
Key rotation does not interrupt active sessions

items.title: Frontend CSP/XSS hardening
items.description: Harden the cockpit frontend against XSS with strict Content Security Policy headers, input sanitization on all projection fields, and automated XSS regression tests. The frontend renders user-provided content (file paths, commit messages, agent outputs) and must not trust any of it.
expected_tests: CSP headers present and restrictive
XSS payload in projection field neutralized
XSS payload in chat message neutralized
XSS payload in file path neutralized

items.title: Static docs public/private split enforcement
items.description: Enforce a public/private split on the static docs renderer so that internal-only JSON artifacts (governance specs, security architecture) are never published to the public GitHub Pages site. The renderer must maintain a denylist of private artifact paths.
expected_tests: Private artifacts excluded from public site
Denylist update triggers renderer reconvergence
Public site does not contain internal-only paths

items.title: Hosted team mode design with Postgres operational substrate
items.description: Design the hosted team mode architecture: Postgres as the operational substrate for multi-tenant coordination, shared session state, and team-level governance. This is the design phase only; implementation comes after the governance spine is proven in single-tenant mode.
expected_tests: Architecture design review completed
Schema design for multi-tenant coordination tables
items.dependency_implications: May require asyncpg or psycopg (not yet added).

items.title: Tenant isolation and RBAC for multi-tenant deployments
items.description: Design and implement tenant isolation with scoped RBAC for multi-tenant deployments. Each tenant must have isolated coordination state, session storage, and tool scoping. Cross-tenant data leakage must be prevented at the storage and API layers.
expected_tests: Tenant A cannot access Tenant B coordination state
Tenant A cannot access Tenant B sessions
RBAC roles enforced per-tenant
Cross-tenant queries blocked at storage layer

items.title: Hosted API airlock for external access
items.description: Design a hosted API airlock that mediates all external access to the Rig Relay control plane in hosted team mode. The airlock must enforce rate limiting, authentication, and content-light scanning before any request reaches the governance spine.
expected_tests: Airlock enforces rate limiting
Airlock enforces authentication before governance spine
Content-light scanning applied to all external requests
Airlock degrades gracefully under load
items.dependency_implications: May require an ASGI server (already available via anyio).

items.title: Enterprise SSO/SCIM planning
items.description: Plan enterprise SSO (OIDC/SAML) and SCIM provisioning integration for hosted team mode. This is a planning-only item; implementation depends on hosted team mode being operational. The plan must cover identity federation, group-to-RBAC mapping, and just-in-time provisioning.
expected_tests: SSO architecture review completed
SCIM provisioning flow documented
Group-to-RBAC mapping designed
items.dependency_implications: No new dependencies at planning stage.

items.title: MCP mutation tools with approval receipt enforcement
items.description: Expose MCP mutation tools (tiers 4 and 5) with mandatory approval receipt enforcement. Every mutation tool call must carry a valid, unexpired approval receipt signed by the governance engine. Without an approval receipt, the tool call is rejected before execution.
expected_tests: Mutation tool without receipt rejected
Expired receipt rejected
Tampered receipt rejected
Valid receipt allows single-use mutation

items.title: A2A federation with remote agent trust tiers
items.description: Implement A2A federation supporting remote agent connections with trust tier-based capability scoping. Remote agents at lower trust tiers get read-only access; higher trust tiers may request mutation with approval receipt. Federation must support agent card discovery and attestation from roadmap-013.
expected_tests: Trust tier 1 remote agent gets read-only access
Trust tier 3 remote agent can request mutation with receipt
Federation handshake validates agent card attestation
Remote agent disconnection cleans up leases

items.title: SSH remote mutation with supervisor wrapping
items.description: Extend the SSH surface from read-only diagnostics to supervised remote mutation. All mutation commands must be wrapped by the RuntimeSupervisor, carry approval receipts, and produce session recordings. This is the highest-risk surface; it must not be implemented before the governance spine is proven.
expected_tests: Mutation command without receipt rejected
Supervisor wraps all mutation commands
Session recording captures full mutation transcript
Supervisor enforces tool permission model

items.title: MCP/ACP/A2A marketplace and ecosystem extensions
items.description: Design a marketplace for community-contributed MCP tools, ACP agent profiles, and A2A agent cards. This is a long-term ecosystem play; the marketplace must enforce the same governance spine as built-in surfaces and require attestation for all third-party contributions.
expected_tests: Marketplace design review completed
Attestation requirement documented for third-party contributions

items.title: Public static site differentiation from internal docs
items.description: Design and implement clear differentiation between the public static site (GitHub Pages) and the internal docs surface. The public site must have a distinct visual identity, a restricted artifact set, and no links to internal governance artifacts. This prevents accidental exposure of internal architecture to public visitors.
expected_tests: Public site does not link to internal governance artifacts
Public site has distinct visual identity
Internal-only paths return 404 on public site

do_not_overrun_guards: Do not implement SSH before authority spine and RuntimeSupervisor wrapping.
Do not implement MCP mutation tools before approval receipts and descriptor integrity.
Do not implement hosted API before tenant/RBAC and Postgres failure semantics.
Do not implement ACP transport before IDE sidecar convergence plan.
Do not implement A2A delegation before Agent Card attestation and trust tiers.
Do not allow CLI/scripts to mutate outside the same governance spine as cockpit.
Do not expose mutation MCP tools to any client without signed, time-bound, scope-bound approval receipts enforced server-side.
Do not deploy static docs without public/private split enforcement and content-light scan.
Do not enable GitHub remote mutation before GitHub Trust Spine v1 prerequisites are satisfied.
Do not implement hosted mode with agent loop or private repo content on server by default.
